pattern.crimePattern: engine-theft fence kills the beach treasurer who matched a stolen outboard to the stolen-engine register
pattern.notes: Fictional BMU, mechanic and serial number (partly masked). Outboard theft on the lake is a well-known problem; no real ring or case is retold.

ob.reportedBy: Dismas Ojwang, chairman, Dunga Beach Management Unit
ob.text: The chairman of Dunga Beach Management Unit reports the BMU treasurer, Phoebe Awuor (44), found dead behind the BMU office among the stored boat engines at about 08:00. She was last seen at the landing in the early morning.

facts.text: Phoebe Awuor, Dunga BMU treasurer, was found dead behind the BMU office among the stored boat engines at about 08:00.
Behind the office: two wounds to her head. The store rack is intact and every engine is still chained in its place.
Levy book, in Phoebe's hand: landings at 06:10, 06:25, 06:40 and 06:52. Nothing after 06:52.
Maurice (KSM-2214): they landed at 07:30. Phoebe always meets every boat at the water with her book. This time she didn't come, and the office door was pulled shut.
Phoebe's omena basket is still full and wet beside her drying net. She always spreads her fish by 07:00.
Benta sold Phoebe her morning chai at 07:05. "She was worried. She said a mechanic was coming to see her."
Benta served chai at her stall from 05:30 to 09:00, with the landing crowd around her.
Seline: Phoebe spreads her own omena on the net by 07:00, every day of her life. Seline found the basket full and wet at 08:00.
Seline was at her stall in the Kisumu fish market from 06:00 to 07:45; her stall receipts are timed.
Stolen-engine register: serial 6Y4-…-1187, stolen at Usenge on 14 October. Phoebe's pencil note: "Elisha's new engine — same number! Geoffrey Ombui sold it. Police post Monday 8am."
Elisha's "reconditioned" engine: fresh grey paint over the old colour, serial plate 6Y4-…-1187.
BMU files: Ombui Marine's last invoice, for servicing the patrol boat, was paid in full on 2 December.
BMU boat register: no boat is registered to Geoffrey Ombui or anyone named Ombui.
Night departure book: Elisha's boat KSM-0871 went out at 04:00 with three crew and landed at 08:15.
Levy reconciliation: the KSh 4,200 shortfall was the chairman's own counting error, found and corrected on Saturday, signed by both.
Records, Geoffrey's line: Dunga mast 07:02–07:29, then Kisumu CBD from 07:45.
Records, Geoffrey's PesaPap: 07:27, KSh 150 to FANUEL OPIYO.
Fanuel: he picked up "the mechanic" outside the BMU office at 07:27. He carried a tool bag and was wet to the knees.
From the shallows behind the office: a three-blade aluminium propeller, "G.O." scratched on the hub, the way Geoffrey marks his workshop stock.
Fisheries sign-in: D. Ojwang, 06:55. The meeting ran from 07:00 to 09:30.
Autopsy: two curved, blade-edged wounds, their spacing consistent with a boat propeller. Clean cut edges; no wood splinters.
Autopsy: no water in the lungs.
Autopsy: death between 06:45 and 08:00.
Autopsy: a healthy heart; no natural disease.
Dr. Chebii: the blade curvature and spacing of the propeller match both wounds.
Geoffrey: "I was at my workshop in town from half past six."
Geoffrey: "That engine was reconditioned from scrap. I have papers."
Geoffrey admits he was in the BMU office with Phoebe from about 07:10, "to explain the papers".
Dismas: "I was at the fisheries office by seven."
Dismas: he and Phoebe quarrelled last week about a levy shortfall. "The numbers were wrong. Mine, not hers."
Elisha: "I was on the lake."
Elisha: he paid Geoffrey KSh 180,000 for the engine. "I didn't know."

interrogations.intro: Geoffrey wipes his hands on a rag at the workshop door. "Phoebe? Pole sana. I was here all morning. Ask anyone."

topics.reply: That engine was reconditioned from scrap. Parts from five engines. Serial numbers on scrap mean nothing, Inspector.
Every mechanic on this lake has propellers. Anyone can scratch two letters.

interrogations.intro: Dismas comes straight from the fisheries meeting, still holding the agenda. "I left her at 06:45 with her book. Go and find who did this."

topics.reply: We fought about numbers last week. The numbers were wrong. Mine, not hers. We fixed it on Saturday.
A propeller? Then it's in the water. My boys dive for dropped engines every week. Give them an hour.

interrogations.intro: Elisha stands by his boat, not looking at the office. "I fish. I came in at quarter past eight and the beach was screaming."

topics.reply: I paid him one hundred and eighty thousand for that engine. My whole savings. I didn't know. I swear I didn't know.

interrogations.intro: Benta pours a glass of chai and pushes it across without asking. "Drink. Then ask."

topics.reply: Every morning, seven o'clock, chai and one mandazi. Today she didn't finish the mandazi. She said a mechanic was coming.

interrogations.intro: Seline sits on an upturned basin by her sister's net. "She spreads her own fish. Every day. Look at the basket."

topics.reply: She talked about that book like it was scripture. Every stolen engine on the lake, she wanted it home.

contradictions.reaction: He puts the rag down. "...I went to Dunga to explain the papers. She wouldn't listen. I left her at her desk."

timeOfDeath.note: The act window: alive buying chai at 07:05, missed the 07:30 landing. The autopsy allows 06:45–08:00.

proof.concludes: Phoebe was alive buying chai at 07:05. At 07:30 she failed to meet KSM-2214, the first landing she ever missed, and her omena was never spread. She died between 07:05 and 07:30.
The engine Geoffrey sold Elisha is a stolen one, serial 1187, and Phoebe had written that she'd take it to the police post at 08:00 on Monday.

Geoffrey wasn't at his workshop: his phone was at Dunga 07:02–07:29, he admits he was in the office from 07:10, and he left on a boda at 07:27 wet to the knees. The propeller in the shallows carries his mark and matches the wounds. Geoffrey Ombui struck Phoebe with a boat propeller because she'd matched his engine to a stolen-engine report.

eliminations.why: She was alive and buying chai at 07:05.
She logged a landing at 06:52 and bought chai at 07:05.
She failed to meet the 07:30 landing; she was already dead.
She missed the 07:30 boat and was found at about 08:00.
Dismas signed in at the county fisheries office at 06:55 and sat in the meeting until 09:30.
Elisha's boat was on the lake from 04:00 until 08:15.
Benta was at her chai stall in front of the landing crowd all morning.
Seline was at her stall in the Kisumu fish market from 06:00.
The rack is intact, every engine still chained, and the wounds are curved blade edges.
Clean blade edges and no wood splinters.
A healthy heart; she was struck twice.
The shortfall was the chairman's error, corrected on Saturday, and it was his quarrel, not Geoffrey's.
The BMU paid Geoffrey's last invoice in full.
That grievance is Elisha's, and Elisha was on the lake.

reconstruction.text: Last week Elisha brings a "reconditioned" 15-horsepower engine to the BMU to register. Phoebe checks the serial against her register: stolen at Usenge in October.
On Sunday she tells Geoffrey Ombui, who sold it, that she'll take it to the beach police post when it opens at 08:00 on Monday.
Monday, 07:05. She buys her chai from Benta and says a mechanic is coming.
07:10. Geoffrey comes to the office to talk her out of it. At about 07:15 he strikes her with a spare propeller from his tool bag, behind the office among the chained engines.

He wades out and drops the propeller in the shallows. At 07:27 he pays a boda rider KSh 150 for a ride to town, wet to the knees. At 07:30 KSM-2214 lands, and for the first time in eleven years nobody meets it with the book.

clockPlan.note: No detention needed; the autopsy and the propeller comparison are immediate. One records request.

ui.beatNotes: The WHEN blank and the timeline rail. The rail slides out from under the corkboard; Benta's 07:05 and the crew's 07:30 snap onto it and the window shades in between them. Mwalimu: "Every fact has a time. Line them up and the gap will tell you."
